clue.text: Vegetable from Spain collected medal

indicators.note: collected in the sense of composed or put together, so the country's letters are set in a new order

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British decoration

explanation.surface: A Spanish grower wins a prize for vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' looks like it means picked up, but it signals a rearrangement; CH stands for Companion of Honour, an order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Old writer's son gets copy before first edition

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An old author's son plagiarises before the first printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'before' order the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a person who copied documents by hand before printing, so a writer of old.

clue.text: Poor Kevin with nothing to call upon

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kevin, being penniless, has nobody to turn to.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for nothing joins Kevin before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To invoke is to appeal to a higher power or authority for help.

clue.text: Decide a map needs to be redrawn by adjutant

indicators.note: redrawing something lays it out afresh, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An officer's assistant is told to decide whether a map should be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who acts as a senior commander's personal assistant, like an adjutant.

clue.text: Establish order within huge crowd

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the words before it

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the second

explanation.surface: Bring control to a vast mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large, often unruly, group of people.

clue.text: Girl pinching posh car gangster's after is bizarre

indicators.note: to pinch is to grab and hold, so the girl's name wraps round what she takes

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, placed after

explanation.surface: A girl stealing a fancy car, with a mobster chasing her, is a strange story.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in gangster's is 'is', and 'after' places him at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something dreamlike and strange, a close synonym of bizarre.

clue.text: Number interviewed without incident

indicators.note: without in its older sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a doctor or employer who has interviewed you has seen you

explanation.surface: A figure was questioned and nothing happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without incident' looks like a phrase meaning smoothly, but 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a number, one more than sixteen.

clue.text: Annoy king by backing priest

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the priest's name is read upwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest from the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: Irritate the monarch by supporting a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's stock priest; 'backing' sounds like supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to irritate or anger them.

clue.text: One leaving country with Russian fighter fled into Egypt

indicators.note: into places what comes before it inside the following word

parts.note: ET is the international code for Egypt
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
to flee is to run away

explanation.surface: A defector escapes in a Russian jet to Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is a person who leaves their home country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Eavesdropper abandoned silent queen

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A snooper deserted a mute queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An eavesdropper is someone secretly listening, an example of a listener.

clue.text: Wandered around Dover

indicators.note: around suggests moving letters about, so the town name is jumbled

parts.note: the Kent port, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strolled about the town of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is a port town in Kent, England; 'around' reads as a preposition but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam aimlessly, so roved is a past-tense synonym of wandered.

clue.text: Valerie, taken in by retired gentleman, has no heart for personal battles

indicators.note: being taken in means being held inside another word
retired means drawn back, so the title is read from the end

parts.note: a title for a gentleman or knight

indicators.note: having no heart means losing the central letter of the name

parts.note: the woman's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: Valerie, adopted by an old gentleman, has a cold streak in her personal feuds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired gentleman' reads as an elderly man, but retired is the signal to turn the title round; 'has no heart' removes only the single central letter of the seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivalries are ongoing contests between competitors, so battles between people.

clue.text: Drug concealed in kebabs and cooked, which may cause flatulence

indicators.note: something concealed in another thing is held within it
cooked means prepared or messed about with, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Narcotics hidden in fast food, then cooked, could give you wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cheeky description rather than a synonym; the drug goes into kebabs, and that plus 'and' is reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked beans, haricot beans in tomato sauce, are famous for producing intestinal gas.

clue.text: Genuine concord initially comes out of ceasefire

indicators.note: coming out of a word means leaving it, so that letter is removed
initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Real harmony first emerges from a halt in fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUCE minus its C.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine are synonyms meaning real or authentic.

clue.text: Toning down F1 practice session

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moderating or restricting a statement
second meaning: the timed laps that set the grid in Formula One

explanation.walkthrough: F1 is Formula One motor racing, whose pre-race timed session decides starting order.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualifying a remark means adding reservations to soften it, and in motor racing qualifying is the session deciding grid positions.

clue.text: Note chapter on Queen struggling with church

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter

indicators.note: struggling suggests something in disarray, so the royal's letters are thrown about

parts.note: the parse needs Queens with an S; the clue as printed has only Queen, the setter's slip
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A musical note marks a chapter about a queen in conflict with the church.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue lacks an S: QUEEN gives only five of the six letters SEQUEN needs, so the setter probably meant 'Queens'. 'Note' is the definition, as in heed or regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequence means importance, as does note in 'a person of note', making them synonyms.

clue.text: Fruit has natural sugar containing antioxidant vitamin

parts.note: nectar is the sugary liquid made by flowers

explanation.surface: A health claim that this fruit is sweet and full of antioxidant vitamins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' looks like a container signal, but it gives the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a fruit.

clue.text: Key to a watering hole in the sky?

definitions.text: Key to a watering hole in the sky?

parts.words: Key to a watering hole in the sky?
parts.note: surface reading: the way into a pub floating among the stars
setter's reading: a key on a keyboard whose name, split, is a pub in outer space

explanation.walkthrough: A watering hole is slang for a pub, and the sky stands for outer space; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key at the bottom of a keyboard inserts a gap between words.

clue.text: Cut short political prisoner's time in cyberspace

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is trimmed off

parts.note: an internee is someone held without trial
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A political detainee's sentence is shortened while online.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after prisoner reads as 'has', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the virtual world of computer networks, the global online network.

clue.text: A man in a cap coming back north on a long waterway

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after what comes before
coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards
in places the man inside the headwear

parts.note: taken as written, placed after the C
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A man in a cap sails home northward along a great waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: A MAN goes inside A CAP after the C to give ACAMANAP, which turns round; N, A and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal is the famous waterway across Central America joining two oceans.

clue.text: Vote for graduate tax to rise

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: a toll is a levy or charge

explanation.surface: A call to vote for raising the tax on graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax to rise' looks like a political slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a vote, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Can't hear without a T loop you first performed with skill

indicators.note: without a says one letter A is taken away
first picks out the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: If you are deaf without a hearing loop, you first handled it skilfully.
explanation.walkthrough: A T loop is a hearing loop for hearing-aid users, which makes 'T loop' look like one item.
explanation.definitionFit: Deftly means neatly and skilfully.

clue.text: Kind of neck band

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a round, close-fitting neckline on a sweater
second meaning: a group of people working together, as on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'neck band' reads as one item of clothing, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew neck is a sweater style, and a crew is a team or gang of workers.

clue.text: French author talked standard English to blend in

indicators.note: talked means the name is said out loud and written as it is pronounced

parts.note: Albert Camus, whose name is pronounced with a silent S
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French writer spoke standard English in order to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard English' looks like one phrase but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Camouflage is disguise that lets something merge with its surroundings, the noun naming the means.

clue.text: Friend's wearing very large gemstones

indicators.note: wearing something means having it round you, so the outer letters enclose

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A mate is sporting enormous jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent precious stones.

clue.text: Scrutinise turnover of new accounts

indicators.note: a turnover flips things, so the letters read the other way

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
ACS is the abbreviation for accounts

explanation.surface: An auditor checks the turnover in fresh accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a business figure from the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine closely, a synonym of scrutinise.

clue.text: Porcelain from good French earth gets a following after feature

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth
the letter a, placed to follow

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain made from good French clay acquires a fan base after being featured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a following after feature' puts A after CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a type of porcelain made with bone ash.

clue.text: Is rented land bounded by water?

explanation.surface: A question about whether leased property has a waterfront.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whole as a riddle; let is the British word for renting out property.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, a piece of land with water all round it.

clue.text: Following Reds' second half drop-off, can United get a point?

indicators.note: the back half of the word dropping off means only its front half stays

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether United can pick up a point after Liverpool collapsed in the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like 'after' but is the definition; 'Reds' is a nickname for Liverpool or Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants accompanying an important person, that is, a following.

clue.text: Lovely to look at place reportedly left unknown

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so a word is spelt to match its sound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A pretty spot, so they say, has been left undiscovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Sightly is the less common positive form of unsightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightly means pleasing to the eye, attractive in appearance.
